claim_verdicts.evidence: db/schema.sql at stage-0, CREATE TABLE order_items: "order_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES orders (id)," and "quantity integer NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0),". So an item row cannot exist without its orders row, and quantity 0 fails the CHECK. Extracted with tools/extract-code db/schema.sql --tag stage-0.

db/seed.sql at stage-0 header: "Fixed data for the lab: 8 products, 5 customers (one of whom never ordered), 12 orders." The orders INSERT lists ids 1..12 and every customer_id in it is 1, 2, 3 or 4 — never 5; customers has "(5, 'Vũ Gia Khánh', 'khanh.vu@example.com', 'Cần Thơ')"; products has "(3, 'Tai nghe', 890000)"; the file ends with setval(pg_get_serial_sequence('orders','id'), 12).

PG17 Tutorial 3.4: "PostgreSQL actually treats every SQL statement as being executed within a transaction. If you do not issue a BEGIN command, then each individual statement has an implicit BEGIN and (if successful) COMMIT wrapped around it." A statement that succeeds is therefore already committed when a later, separate statement fails.

PG17 BEGIN, Description: "all statements after a BEGIN command will be executed in a single transaction until an explicit COMMIT or ROLLBACK is given." Notes add: "Issuing BEGIN when already inside a transaction block will provoke a warning message. The state of the transaction is not affected."

PG17 COMMIT, Description: "COMMIT commits the current transaction. All changes made by the transaction become visible to others and are guaranteed to be durable if a crash occurs." For the other ending, Tutorial 3.4: "we can issue the command ROLLBACK instead of COMMIT, and all our updates so far will be canceled."

PG17 13.2.1 (Read Committed is the default level): a SELECT "sees only data committed before the query began; it never sees either uncommitted data or changes committed by concurrent transactions during the query's execution" and "However, SELECT does see the effects of previous updates executed within its own transaction, even though they are not yet committed." Tutorial 3.4: "The updates made so far by an open transaction are invisible to other transactions until the transaction completes."

PG17 COMMIT, Description: changes "are guaranteed to be durable if a crash occurs." Glossary, Durability: "The assurance that once a transaction has been committed, the changes remain even after a system failure or crash." The lab sets no asynchronous-commit option, so the default guarantee applies.

PG17 protocol, ReadyForQuery status byte: "'E' if in a failed transaction block (queries will be rejected until block is ended)" — that is the 'rejects every further command' half. For the other half: Glossary, Atomicity: "The property of a transaction that either all its operations complete as a single unit or none do"; §53.2.2.1 notes an error leaves "the session ... inside a failed regular transaction block", which no ending can keep. The savepoint exception recorded in the claim is correct (SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO exist for exactly this) and is not taught in the lesson.

PG17 protocol, Termination (53.2.9): "For either normal or abnormal termination, any open transaction is rolled back, not committed." psql, Exit Status: it returns "3 if an error occurred in a script and the variable ON_ERROR_STOP was set" — psql leaves at that error without sending ROLLBACK, so the block still open is rolled back by the server when the connection goes.

PG17 13.3.2 Row-Level Locks: "other transactions that attempt UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT FOR UPDATE, SELECT FOR NO KEY UPDATE, SELECT FOR SHARE or SELECT FOR KEY SHARE of these rows will be blocked until the current transaction ends", and "Row-level locks are released at transaction end or during savepoint rollback, just like table-level locks."

PG17 Glossary, ACID: "Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability. This set of properties of database transactions is intended to guarantee validity in concurrent operation and even in event of errors, power failures, etc."

Derived from the pinned files, not executed — Docker Desktop is not running on this machine and no psql client is installed, so the lab could not be started. db/seed.sql puts exactly 12 rows in orders (ids 1..12), so orders_before is 12; the block inserts orders id 13 and counts on the same connection, which by 13.2.1 "does see the effects of previous updates executed within its own transaction" → 13; ROLLBACK discards it (Tutorial 3.4: "all our updates so far will be canceled") → 12.

scripts/sql/run-query.sh at stage-0: "psql --host db --username donhang --dbname donhang --no-psqlrc --echo-queries --set ON_ERROR_STOP=on --file \"/repo/db/queries/${query}.sql\"" — one psql invocation, one --file. PG17 psql states the effect of the variable: "If any individual query fails, execution of the remaining queries continues unless ON_ERROR_STOP is set", and Exit Status "3 if an error occurred in a script and the variable ON_ERROR_STOP was set."

PG17 BEGIN, Notes: "Statements are executed more quickly in a transaction block, because transaction start/commit requires significant CPU and disk activity." 14.4.1 Disable Autocommit: "When using multiple INSERTs, turn off autocommit and just do one commit at the end... If you allow each insertion to be committed separately, PostgreSQL is doing a lot of work for each row that is added."

Both halves hold. 13.3.2: other transactions attempting UPDATE/DELETE/SELECT FOR UPDATE etc. on those rows "will be blocked until the current transaction ends"; and "Row-level locks do not affect data querying; they block only writers and lockers to the same row" — so a plain reader is answered at once. The 'keep it short' half carries its condition (a block held open waiting for something outside the database), so it is not an unconditioned recommendation.

db/queries/write-basics.sql at stage-0: BEGIN; then INSERT INTO products ... RETURNING, UPDATE products SET price_vnd = 300000, DELETE FROM products WHERE name = 'Túi đựng laptop'; then ROLLBACK. Three writes, all between BEGIN and ROLLBACK. Extracted with tools/extract-code db/queries/write-basics.sql --tag stage-0.

The sentence is true — PG17 CREATE SEQUENCE, Notes: "Because nextval and setval calls are never rolled back, sequence objects cannot be used if 'gapless' assignment of sequence numbers is needed" — but it is a hidden claim.
